topics.topic: Durable authority and ownership for the audit sequence high-water mark across failed changes, erasure, and restore
questions: What durable fact or authority remembers the greatest sequence number ever minted when entries have been erased or the store is restored from a backup that predates later minting, and which model owns that fact?
What durable fact preserves the greatest sequence number ever minted, including numbers from uncommitted changes, so restoring an older store cannot mint one again?
What durable instance fact tells Registry the greatest sequence number ever minted, including numbers absent from the restored store and numbers allocated for changes that did not commit?

quotes:
Sequence numbers are never reused (M09). Changes that write an entry are
   applied one at a time. Before such a change commits, Registry records its
   number in the instance marks — a small file in the backup location, apart
   from the store and the backups, which a restore does not replace (A18); a
   change that then fails leaves its number unused for ever, and the log
   skips it. At start Registry continues above the higher of the store's
   last number and the marks'. Marks that are missing are made from the
   store's last number, with a diagnostic: only a loss of the marks together
   with a restore could lower the numbering, and that is outside Registry's
   guarantees (A18 rule 10).
judgement.why: State 2 assigns the durable high-water mark to the instance-marks file, preserves it across store restoration, and defines recovery when it is missing.

topics.topic: MigrationClosure persistence and import eligibility before a checked backup contains the closure
questions: Between successful import and the first checked backup containing the MigrationClosure, may an older backup without the closure be restored, and if not, what fact or lifecycle rule prevents that restoration and a second import?
After the import succeeds but before a checked backup containing the closure exists, may restoring an older backup remove the MigrationClosure and reopen the one-time import?

After a successful import but before a backup containing the MigrationClosure has passed its check, may restoring an older backup make the closure absent and permit the one-time import again, or must the closure remain present throughout that interval?

quotes:
None; absent, then present forever: once a backup holding it has passed its
check, no backup without it is kept (State 2 A16, A18).

An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction. The import has succeeded when that transaction
   is committed; Registry knows it by the closure.

While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused
   (R0-79).

Right after an accepted import Registry makes a backup run outside the
   daily schedule (A18). Once a backup holding the closure has passed its
   check, Registry deletes every backup made before the import, so no kept
   backup can bring back a store without the closure (M10). Until then a
   failed run is retried at the next run; the import stays accepted.

Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions): the owner decrypts it
   with the key it was made with, kept in the vault (rule 3). It is started by
   the release that made it, or by a later release after that release's own
   store migration (A17 rule 5). Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it; the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever minted (A15). Every kept
   backup made after the import holds its closure (A16 rule 10), so the
   import stays closed (R0-79).

Its guarantee after a restore is what the backup
   held.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits restoration of a still-kept pre-import backup before the new checked backup exists, removing the closure and allowing another import; another forbids such restoration or preserves the closure independently so the import remains closed. The owner notices whether the one-time import becomes available again.
judgement.why: The texts promise that the closure is permanent and the import stays accepted, but they neither forbid restoration of the pre-import backups retained during this interval nor identify any independent fact that preserves the closure through such a restore.

topics.topic: Whether and when failed or uncommitted changes may advance the audit sequence allocator
questions: Is advancing the audit sequence allocator an explicit exception to the guarantees that a refused or uncommitted change changes nothing and that every change is atomic, and exactly which failed attempts may advance it?
